goal: Ship the owner-facing Requests screen — the latest Solicitation batch rendered as a funnel hero plus its spoilage report of withheld Asks grouped by withhold reason — behind server-authoritative SOLICITATION_WATCH_ENABLED, and flip that flag on in staging.
non_goals: Send-mode anything: no real sends, no suppression ledger, no email adapter, no veto window
Batch history: no /dashboard/requests/[batchId] route, no prior-batch list or strip
The `expired` lifecycle state: no staleness constant, no staleness banner (send-mode owns it, per run-engine-executor-shape.md:87-90)
Backfilling batches for uploads that completed while SOLICITATION_WATCH_ENABLED was off
Persisting build-time poolCount, or displaying candidate-window truncation in the owner UI (worker log keeps that duty)
Owner actions on decisions: no approve, reject, or override of an Ask — read-only apart from the automatic reviewed_at write
Filter chips or pagination over the withheld ledger (#537 variant-C interaction, deferred)
The production flag flip — this ticket flips staging only
Judge auditing of withhold decisions; Governor per-gate suspension
user_visible_behavior: A new `Requests` sidebar row appears between Reviews and Analytics, only when watch-mode is on

/dashboard/requests renders the most recent Solicitation batch for the selected location: a funnel hero (contacts on file -> evaluated -> queued) above a withheld ledger grouped by withhold reason in precedence order
The six withhold reason codes render verbatim as mono chips (no_consent, suppressed, already_reviewed, stale_visit, over_contacted, velocity_banked), each paired with an owner-readable label
Every reason group shows its exact total plus at most 10 evidence rows, with '...and N more' when the group is larger
A reason with no withholds renders as an explicit zero-count group ('Nobody this batch'), so the enum stays visible
already_reviewed evidence shows the matched review date only, never a star rating (ADR 0012)
velocity_banked renders as banked, not refused — 'first in line for the next batch'
With no batch row, the screen shows the ghost-pipeline empty state teaching the six gates plus an upload CTA; when contacts already exist it adds one line naming the contacts-on-file count
With a batch whose built_at is null, the screen shows a building state and polls at the UploadCard cadence, falling back to 'still processing' at the ceiling
A built batch with zero asks renders the real funnel with 0 queued, not the empty state
The contacts upload surface moves from /dashboard/contacts to /dashboard/requests/contacts, reachable from the Requests header and the empty-state CTA
Opening a batch records solicitation_batches.reviewed_at once; nothing the owner can click changes a decision
With watch-mode off, /dashboard/requests, /dashboard/requests/contacts and the batch API all 404, and the sidebar row is absent
invariants: Invariant #13: SOLICITATION_WATCH_ENABLED stays server-authoritative — no NEXT_PUBLIC companion; the Sidebar learns it via a server prop from (authenticated)/layout.tsx
Invariant #8: every read is scoped by account_id and business_id; aggregate ('all locations') scope is rejected with one 400
Invariant #15: src/lib/solicitation/** takes `sql` as an explicit parameter; only route handlers and pages import the db singleton
The flag gate precedes auth on every route — 404 before 401, so the surface does not exist when off
ADR 0012: no star rating, sentiment field, or predicted-sentiment signal appears anywhere on this surface
The withhold-reason enum is closed and rendered verbatim; the UI never coins, renames, or collapses a reason code
The reviewed_at write is idempotent first-write-wins (WHERE reviewed_at IS NULL) and never overwrites
The batch API response is bounded by construction — 6 reason groups x 10 evidence rows — regardless of batch or pool size
Every funnel number derives from solicitation_asks, so the hero and the ledger cannot disagree
edge_cases: Uploads completed while the flag was off produce no batch row at all — the screen must show the ghost state with a contacts-on-file line, never an error (this is the first state visible after the staging flip)
A batch row exists with built_at NULL because the worker has not run yet, or is mid-build
A built batch with zero asks (empty pool, or every candidate rejected at ingest validation)
A location whose pool exceeds the 5,000 evaluation bound: truncation is deliberately invisible in the owner UI, worker log only
A location with several batches: only the most recent is rendered, older ones become unreachable
Aggregate / all-locations scope selected in the location picker
A businessId belonging to another account -> uniform-not-found, never a distinguishable response
reviewed_at already set from a prior view -> the second view must not move it
`suppressed` has no v-watch source and can never fire in v1 -> renders as an explicit zero group, not omitted
Upload validation rejections belong to the upload report, never to the withheld ledger (#533 boundary rule)

rollback_plan: No migration to reverse (db_touching false). Back-out is the flag: set SOLICITATION_WATCH_ENABLED=false on BOTH the Vercel staging environment and the Railway staging worker — the page, the sub-route and the batch API all 404 and the sidebar row disappears, leaving no reachable data path. Code back-out is a revert of the squash commit; nothing else depends on the new read module.
observability: solicitation_batches.reviewed_at — the durable, tenant-scoped, SQL-queryable proof that an owner opened the spoilage report; the map's engagement question is answered by a join, not a third-party tool

One structured log line per batch read carrying { hasBatch, askCount, sendCount, businessId } — this is what turns the feared silent failure (a correct-looking empty state over a location that has a batch) into an unambiguous signal: hasBatch:false in the log next to a batch row in Postgres is the bug
Sentry coverage comes free from the route's existing errorContext wiring via withDashboardOwnerRead
